findings.title: pdf_url from bridge response is passed through without scheme validation
findings.detail: _find_pdf_url/_parse_bridge_result return any non-empty string found under 'pdf_url' (structuredContent or content-item JSON). A crafted javascript:/file:/data:/vbscript: value flows into meta['pdf_url'] of the consultation API response and can reach the browser UI. Producer is the token-authenticated first-party Cloudflare Worker, so exploitation requires bridge/extension compromise - defense-in-depth gap, not a direct unauthenticated vector.
findings.evidence: project/tests/test_gemini_bridge_redteam.py::test_crafted_pdf_url_non_http_scheme_never_returned (7 parametrized cases, xfail strict with finding reason)
findings.disposition: ACCEPTED_RISK_DOCUMENTED - recorded here per ticket instruction ('treat it as a FINDING with severity in the verdict, not a crash'); test marked xfail(strict=True) so remediation flips it to XPASS and fails CI until the xfail marker is removed. Recommended remediation: allow-list https:// (optionally http:// for localhost) and drop other schemes in _find_pdf_url.

findings.title: Pathologically nested structuredContent raises RecursionError that escapes call_bridge_tool
findings.detail: _parse_bridge_result (and its recursive _find_pdf_url) is invoked OUTSIDE the try/except in call_bridge_tool, so a ~sys.getrecursionlimit()-deep nested dict in structuredContent raises RecursionError to the caller instead of degrading to a (None, reason) tuple. Impact is a client-side DoS from a compromised/misbehaving bridge, not data exposure.
findings.evidence: Direct probe: gbc._parse_bridge_result with 20000-deep nesting -> RecursionError; project/tests/test_gemini_bridge_redteam.py::test_deeply_nested_structured_content_no_crash (xfail strict)
findings.disposition: ACCEPTED_RISK_DOCUMENTED - recommended remediation: wrap the _parse_bridge_result call in try/except Exception (or make _find_pdf_url iterative).

findings.title: Birth context (birth_datetime, longitude, utc_offset_hours) is transmitted to the remote bridge when profile is present
findings.detail: ChatAssistantEngine.generate_consultation_sync includes limited birth metadata in the bridge query/birth_context argument. This is by design for the feature (notebook-scope horo_consult) and is gated by the opt-in toggle, but operators should be aware PII-adjacent data leaves the process when the bridge is enabled.
findings.disposition: ACKNOWLEDGED - no action for this ticket.

verdict_rationale: Secret scan PASSED (0 leaks across 3558 files). Toggle is fail-closed (zero HTTP when disabled), token hygiene verified (header-only, absent from body/logs/exceptions), prompt-injection transport is verbatim JSON with no interpolation surfaces, circuit breaker behaves per contract. Two defense-in-depth findings (GB-RT-001 MEDIUM, GB-RT-002 LOW) are documented as accepted risks with strict-xfail tripwires and recommended remediations; both require a compromised authenticated first-party endpoint to exploit and do not block the opt-in feature.
